findings.text: Provides debugger read and write access to the task FPSIMD vector and control image. Reads synchronize from effective state before exporting the stored user view. Writes refresh from effective state, merge caller bytes into a copy, store it back, then synchronize toward effective state with zero padding and flush cached task state. Public wrappers reject when the platform lacks support and preserve live state when tracing self.

Exposes two thread local slots through debugger access. Reads preserve live state when target is self, then export the primary pointer value plus either the second hardware pointer when supported or zeros otherwise. Writes start from current stored values, merge caller supplied bytes, and update the stored slots while honoring platform support for the second slot.

Exposes a single floating point mode register per thread. Reads preserve live state for self and export the stored value. Writes merge caller bytes into the stored value and flush task state so the new mode takes effect. Both directions reject when the platform lacks the feature.

Exposes the saved system call number from the task trap frame. Reads return the stored number. Writes update the stored number from caller bytes over the full integer range and then resynchronize the saved first argument used for restart handling when the number changed from the no call sentinel.

Provides common debugger access for scalable vector state in both non streaming and streaming modes, with thin wrappers selecting the vector kind and enforcing feature support. The read path builds a header from task state, exports the header, then either stops for inactive type, delegates to FPSIMD handling for FPSIMD encoding, or exports scalable registers plus status registers with zero padding. The write path validates a caller header, adjusts vector length, allocates storage, enters or exits streaming mode, clears legacy state, then installs either FPSIMD or scalable payload.

Provides debugger access to matrix and lookup table extensions. Matrix reads export a header describing vector length and active size, followed by matrix bytes when enabled and zero padding. Matrix writes set vector length, ensure backing storage, disable the unit when no payload remains, otherwise validate length match and install bytes while marking the unit active. Table reads report zeros when the matrix unit is inactive and stored bytes otherwise; writes ensure storage and on success mark the matrix unit active.

Exposes pointer authentication configuration. One accessor exports data and instruction masks derived from the user mask when address authentication is supported. Another exports and updates the enabled key bitmap through dedicated helpers constrained by an allowed mask. Address and generic key sets export and install wide key material by converting between kernel split halves and user wide integers, starting from current stored keys and merging caller bytes.

Exposes memory tagging control and permission overlay state. Tagging control reads through a helper that may report an error sentinel and writes by merging caller bytes then applying through a setter helper. Overlay reads refresh the stored value from hardware when tracing self and exports it, while writes merge caller bytes into the stored value. Overlay access rejects when the platform lacks support.

Debugger operations fail cleanly when the required hardware capability is absent. FPSIMD, floating mode, scalable vector, streaming matrix, second generation matrix, address versus generic authentication, and overlay features are each checked before access, with unsupported requests rejected and no state changed. Scalable vector writes additionally accept an FPSIMD encoded header with zero length on machines without vector support to allow leaving streaming mode.

When the traced target is the current task, reads first preserve live hardware state into the thread image so the exported view reflects recent execution. This applies to FPSIMD, thread pointers, floating mode, scalable headers, matrix state and overlay state, the latter by rereading the hardware register directly.

Scalable header construction reports register encoding, vector length inheritance, current and maximum lengths, and payload sizes. The task streaming flag selects whether scalable or streaming type is considered active. Active tasks using scalable state report scalable encoding, otherwise FPSIMD encoding is reported. Inheritance flag mirrors the corresponding thread flag for the requested type. Current length comes from the task, maximum from the platform. Active size reflects full payload for the length and encoding, inactive size is header only, and maximum size assumes scalable encoding at maximum length.

Scalable reads always start with a fixed header. When reported size equals header size no further register bytes are shown, preventing leakage across modes. FPSIMD encoding delegates remaining output to the FPSIMD reader. Scalable encoding exports the saved scalable bytes up to the fault register area, then zeros a reserved gap, then exports status registers from the stored control area, then zeros trailing padding to the rounded size.

Scalable writes flush task state, require at least a header, and validate encoding against requested type, rejecting FPSIMD encoding for streaming type. Nonzero length triggers vector length configuration with caller flags after masking encoding bits; zero length is only allowed without vector support and requires pure FPSIMD encoding. Storage is allocated for streaming and scalable use as needed, streaming mode is entered or exited with corresponding thread flags, legacy vector and control state is cleared, FPSIMD payload installs through the FPSIMD writer with state marked FPSIMD, while scalable payload requires length match when data is present and installs register and control ranges while ignoring a reserved gap.

Matrix enablement governs visibility and retention. Reads show header only when disabled and full storage when enabled, with trailing padding zeroed. Writes allocate streaming and matrix storage, preserving existing matrix bytes only when already enabled, disable the unit when the caller supplies header only, reject length mismatch when payload is present, and enable the unit on successful install. Table state reads as zero when matrix is disabled and writes allocate storage as needed, enabling matrix on success.

Scalable debugger header carries encoding and inheritance flags, current vector length, maximum vector length, current payload size and maximum payload size. Size fields allow a debugger to distinguish header only inactive views from full register views and to size buffers for the largest supported configuration.

Related debugger views use small fixed layouts. Matrix header carries flags, current and maximum lengths, and current and maximum sizes with header only size indicating disabled state. Authentication mask view carries separate data and instruction masks. Address key view carries four wide keys for instruction and data keys, generic view carries one wide key. Thread pointer view carries two 64 bit slots. Tagging, key enable and overlay views each carry a single control word.

Payload offsets are anchored to header size: FPSIMD and scalable payloads both begin immediately after the scalable header, and matrix payload begins immediately after the matrix header. Scalable register area extends to the end of the fault register region for the current length, followed by a reserved gap before status registers and trailing padding rounded to vector quadword granularity. Matrix total size is a function of length, and table register size is a fixed byte count.
Pointer authentication keys are presented to userspace as wide integers formed by placing the high half in the upper bits and the low half in the lower bits, with the reverse split on install.

Several paths guard against stale or cross mode data. FPSIMD updates synchronize from effective state before merging so short writes cannot resurrect old bytes. Scalable reads suppress register bytes when the requested type is inactive. Scalable and matrix writes reject register install when the effective length differs from the requested length while payload remains. Tagging and key enable helpers can return error sentinels that are propagated rather than exported.

State changing writes handle backing storage explicitly. Streaming allocation preserves existing matrix state while scalable allocation can clear existing scalable state. Missing storage after allocation attempts fails with out of memory. Successful scalable mode selection always clears legacy vector registers and status registers before installing new payload.
